\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Noise.Polynomial}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of Gaussian affine monomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussian_affine_monomial}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_gaussian_affine_monomial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $a\in\mathbb R^n$, let $s\in\mathbb R$, and let
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a finite set of coordinates. The function
$y\mapsto\prod_{i\in S}(a_i+s y_i)$ is integrable under the product of $n$ standard
Gaussian measures.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian integral of an affine monomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussian_affine_monomial}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_gaussian_affine_monomial}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $a\in\mathbb R^n$, let $s\in\mathbb R$, and let
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be any subset of coordinates. For $Y$ with the product
standard Gaussian law on $\mathbb R^n$, $\mathbb E\left[\prod_{i\in
S}(a_i+sY_i)\right]=\prod_{i\in S}a_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial evaluation is Gaussian-integrable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_eval_gaussian}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_eval_gaussian}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\mathbb K$ be a complete normed field equal to
$\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $P$ be a polynomial in $n$ variables with
coefficients in $\mathbb K$. For every exponent $p\in[0,\infty]$ other than $\infty$,
the function on $\mathbb R^n$ obtained by evaluating $P$ at the coordinatewise images of
$x$ in $\mathbb K$ belongs to $L^p$ for the product standard Gaussian measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Real polynomial representing a real part]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_real_polynomial_re}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_real_polynomial_re}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $P$ be a polynomial in $n$ variables with complex
coefficients. There is a polynomial $Q$ in $n$ variables with real coefficients such
that, for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $Q(x)$ equals the real part of $P(x)$, where $P$ is
evaluated using the complex coordinates of $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial representation of a linear map]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_polynomial_eval_linear}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_polynomial_eval_linear}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $L\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb C$ be a continuous
real-linear map. There is a polynomial $P$ in $n$ variables with complex coefficients
such that, for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, evaluating $P$ at the complex coordinates of $x$
gives $L(x)$.
\end{lemma}
